description: Two RDS DB instances that explicitly request a public endpoint. CustomerDatabase declares PubliclyAccessible: true while also declaring a DB subnet group of private subnets, so the template contradicts itself and the property decides the outcome. TelemetryDatabase declares the same property on a different engine, which shows the defect belongs to the request and not to postgres. rules/public-access/rds_publicly_accessible.guard only inspects the property where it is declared, because CloudFormation otherwise derives the default from the subnet group and an absent value is not evidence of a public endpoint; both instances therefore declare it. Both are otherwise correctly configured: storage encryption enabled, a seven day backup retention window, deletion protection enabled, and Environment and Owner tags. No security group is declared, deliberately: an ingress rule open to 0.0.0.0/0 is the NetworkSecurity defect case-005 measures, and one here would make this case measure two categories at once. The master password is managed by RDS rather than declared, so the template contains no credential.

expected_findings.note: PubliclyAccessible: true on the DB instance, reported by the rds_publicly_accessible Guard rule. Severity CRITICAL comes from the per-rule entry in rules/public-access/_meta.json rather than from that category's HIGH default.

PubliclyAccessible: true on the second DB instance, reported by the same rds_publicly_accessible Guard rule. Two separate resources, so two findings: deduplication merges on resource plus category and these differ in the resource.
